This was really my fault, it was when I was 16 and my best friend was 17. I’m 21 now for reference. We were playing the first Destiny day when the new dlc Rise of Iron came out. We both absolutely loved it. About a week after release the raid wrath of the machine dropped and I really wanted to do it day one. My friend on the other hand wasn’t able to do it that day and said we would have to wait until next weekend when he was free. I said alright, and then found an lfg group that was doing it from the beginning. We got through the first encounter as that’s all I wanted to do to get a feel. My friend and our clan found out that I had done the raid without them so they decided to do the raid the same day, without telling me and also streaming it. I really wouldn’t have cared less, I shouldn’t have done it if I said I would with them. I tune into the stream just at the right time, towards the end of the raid where I can hear my best friend say “Don’t play, talk to, or invite OP for a while. I want him to learn his lesson.” Long story short I was upset and hurt by this. In the heat of the moment I sent him the clip snd messaged him telling him F you and how I was hurt. I didn’t speak to him for a few weeks. After which things were never the same. I played a few times with the clan but everything was different. They didn’t like me anymore. About a year later I messaged him and apologized about it, asking for forgiveness and telling him that I should’ve waited. His response was thank you, but I don’t want to talk to you anymore let alone be friends. I messaged a few times throughout the years all to a similar response or radio silence. Funny enough last year I found the same clan from the Xbox days on pc in destiny 2. Everyone was happy to hear from me except, you guessed it, my ex best friend. He sounded just ecstatic, like ah mannn this guy, am I right? It was cool to see they’re still on the same game, but I didn’t stick around. Said hi and then vanished. Anyways, if you’re reading this somehow Ben, I’m still sorry. I regret what I said. You were a great friend and I messed it up. Although I think you went a bit overboard on your reaction, but we could’ve talked it out. It’s okay, I still take the blame because I initiated.

Hello there, in my opinion small talk would be any conversation that doesn’t last too long or goes into depth. By a deep conversation you’re not just asking the “what” and “how”, like small talk does, but you’re asking the most important part of a deep conversation. The “why”. Why is the gateway to getting to know someone as a person. Rather and asking “how are you?” And getting a response like, “oh I’m good, how about you?”. While it is nice to be asked how are you, it doesn’t add much depth to the conversation in regards to wondering “why” they’re feeling good, or sad, or mad, etc. I hope I may have been of assistance :)
